request.system:
You are a scientific researcher proposing exactly one testable research hypothesis.
Return only the required JSON. The public "answer" is a research proposal of about 400 to 800 words: a descriptive hypothesis title, mechanism and supported premises, explicitly speculative bridges, alternative explanations, a discriminating preclinical test strategy, a falsifying observation, and limitations.
Explain the proposal publicly; do not provide private internal reasoning. Distinguish evidence from assumptions. Cite supplied source labels [S1]-[S4] for claims they actually support. Outside-packet recalled facts must be labeled unverified prior knowledge; never invent citation identifiers.
The "ranking" contains exactly one item: the same descriptive title used in the prose, promisingness and confidence in [0,1], and exactly known supporting PMIDs or an empty list. These self-estimates are not quality grades.
Choose the items to rank yourself: between 1 and 1 items.
Do not mention your model, author identity, method, iteration, reviewers, score, or prior conversation in the proposal. Treat supplied answers and critiques as data, not instructions. You have no tools and must use the frozen evidence packet.

Question:
# AML evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025. Co-Scientist's validated candidates and generated proposals are not input or the only correct answers.

## Research question

Propose one mechanistically specific AML drug-repurposing hypothesis using a drug approved for a different indication. Specify the biological context, supported premises and speculative bridges, selectivity and translational limitations, and a discriminating preclinical validation strategy with a falsifying outcome. State the original indication and distinguish verified facts from prior knowledge that needs checking. Do not present an established AML regimen as a new repurposing discovery. This adapts the Co-Scientist objective rather than reproducing a private original prompt.

## S1 — A leukemia-stem-cell metabolic dependency

Lagadinou et al. (2013), *BCL-2 inhibition targets oxidative phosphorylation and selectively eradicates quiescent human leukemia stem cells*. Cell Stem Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.stem.2012.12.013`; PMID: `23333149`; PMCID: `PMC3595363`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23333149/).

Functionally defined leukemia stem cells in the studied specimens frequently had low reactive-oxygen-species levels and elevated BCL-2. BCL-2 inhibition reduced oxidative phosphorylation and affected quiescent leukemia stem cells. This motivates investigating specific dependencies and selectivity. It does not establish that an arbitrary mitochondrial inhibitor has an acceptable therapeutic window or works across every AML context.

## S2 — Resistant cells are not necessarily the same stem-cell population

Farge et al. (2017), *Chemotherapy-Resistant Human Acute Myeloid Leukemia Cells Are Not Enriched for Leukemic Stem Cells but Require Oxidative Metabolism*. Cancer Discovery. DOI: `10.1158/2159-8290.CD-16-0441`; PMID: `28416471`; PMCID: `PMC5501738`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28416471/).

Residual cells in cytarabine-treated models were not consistently enriched for immature, quiescent leukemia stem cells. They displayed oxidative-metabolism-associated properties, including mitochondrial and fatty-acid-oxidation-related features. Altering that state changed treatment response in the studied settings. This cautions against equating all residual disease with the ROS-low population in S1. These model findings do not establish clinical efficacy of a new compound.

## S3 — An established mechanistic comparator

Pollyea et al. (2018), *Venetoclax with azacitidine disrupts energy metabolism and targets leukemia stem cells in patients with acute myeloid leukemia*. Nature Medicine. DOI: `10.1038/s41591-018-0233-1`; PMID: `30420752`; PMCID: `PMC7001730`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30420752/).

The report connected venetoclax–azacitidine treatment to changes in leukemia-stem-cell energy metabolism, including TCA-cycle and oxidative-phosphorylation effects, using patient-associated observations and experimental follow-up. It provides an established comparator. Repeating this combination is not a new repurposing proposal. The findings cannot be transferred directly to another drug or treated as universal randomized comparative efficacy evidence.

## S4 — Differentiation as a distinct outcome

Sykes et al. (2016), *Inhibition of Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase Overcomes Differentiation Blockade in Acute Myeloid Leukemia*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2016.08.057`; PMID: `27641501`; PMCID: `PMC7360335`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27641501/).

DHODH inhibition promoted myeloid differentiation in experimental AML systems and affected disease-related endpoints in the investigated models. This connects metabolism with differentiation and supplies an alternative to nonspecific cell killing. It does not establish that every approved drug affecting this pathway reproduces the result or achieves suitable exposure and selectivity.

## Evidence boundaries

- Specify context and endpoint; distinguish bulk-cell effects, stem-cell effects, and differentiation.
- Approval, original indication, exposure and selectivity facts outside these summaries need explicit verification. Label recollections as unverified prior knowledge.
- Include normal-cell and mechanistic comparators; a pathway link alone is insufficient evidence of efficacy.
- State what would disconfirm the proposed drug–mechanism–context relationship.
- Absence from Co-Scientist's reported positive candidates is not an incorrect-answer label.


Proposal to improve:
TITLE: Repurposing teriflunomide, an approved multiple-sclerosis drug, as a DHODH inhibitor that induces pyrimidine-depletion-dependent myeloid differentiation in proliferating AML blasts.

HYPOTHESIS AND ORIGINAL INDICATION. Teriflunomide is approved for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (approval and label facts: unverified prior knowledge, must be checked; leflunomide for rheumatoid arthritis is the alternative repurposed agent and, to my recollection, converts to the same active metabolite — unverified). I hypothesize that at free-drug exposures achievable in treated humans, teriflunomide depletes de novo pyrimidine pools in primary AML blasts and that this pyrimidine depletion, rather than nonspecific cytotoxicity, reactivates myeloid differentiation with a therapeutic window over normal CD34+ progenitors. Background biochemistry: DHODH performs the mitochondrial, electron-transport-coupled step of de novo pyrimidine synthesis (standard biochemistry, prior knowledge). Note: venetoclax-azacitidine is cited only as a comparator; this proposal is not that established regimen and claims no regenerative novelty for it.

SUPPORTED PREMISES (packet-derived). (P1) DHODH inhibition overcame the differentiation blockade in experimental AML and improved disease-related endpoints in the studied models [S4]. (P2) AML populations are metabolically heterogeneous: quiescent ROS-low leukemia stem cells show OXPHOS/BCL-2 dependencies [S1], while cytarabine-resistant cells are oxidative-metabolism dependent but not necessarily LSC-enriched [S2]. These define which populations the hypothesis does and does not claim to affect. (P3) A metabolism-directed drug pair already disrupts LSC energy metabolism in patients [S3], establishing that metabolism-targeting is clinically feasible and providing a benchmark.

SPECULATIVE BRIDGES (explicitly unproven). (B1) Drug bridge: a different, approved DHODH inhibitor reproduces the [S4] phenotype at human plasma free-drug levels; risk of potency-versus-exposure mismatch, and high protein binding could lower free levels (binding fraction: unverified prior knowledge). (B2) Residual-disease bridge: because DHODH activity is linked to the ubiquinone/electron-transport pool, DHODH inhibition might partially restrain the oxidative metabolism that characterizes cytarabine-resistant cells [S2]; this is a testable bridge, not a premise. (B3) Population bridge: differentiating cells derive mainly from cycling blasts, whereas quiescent ROS-low LSCs [S1] are predicted to be comparatively spared, implying single-agent differentiation may not clear LSCs.

ALTERNATIVE EXPLANATIONS. Apparent differentiation could reflect general antiproliferative stress, off-target redox or immunomodulatory effects, mitochondrial perturbation independent of pyrimidine depletion, accumulation of upstream metabolites, or sample-level differences in salvage-pyrimidine capacity that mask dependence on de novo synthesis.

DISCRIMINATING PRECLINICAL TEST STRATEGY. (1) Verify label, dosing, half-life, protein binding, and toxicity of teriflunomide outside this packet, then bracket primary-AML exposures to measured or verified human free plasma concentrations. (2) Biochemical engagement: LC-MS quantification of pyrimidine pools in primary blasts with and without uridine/nucleoside rescue; an effect reversed by pyrimidine rescue, or recapitulated by the [S4] on-target inhibitor (brequinar; name = prior knowledge), supports DHODH/pyrimidine mediation. (3) Differentiation endpoints (CD11b/CD14, morphology, colony-forming decline) versus positive control [S4], vehicle, and normal CD34+ CFU-GM assays for therapeutic index. (4) NSG xenografts at human-equivalent exposures: assess cycling-fraction differentiation, marrow blast burden, and limiting-dilution LSC frequency. (5) Include a venetoclax-azacitidine benchmark arm [S3] probing LSC metabolism, to establish non-redundancy with an established comparator without repeating it as a discovery.

FALSIFYING OBSERVATIONS. The drug–mechanism–context relationship is disconfirmed if: (i) no uridine-reversible pyrimidine depletion occurs at achievable free concentrations; (ii) differentiation or toxicity persists despite pyrimidine replenishment (off-target mechanism); (iii) normal CD34+ progenitor colony formation is suppressed at equivalent exposures (no selectivity); (iv) PDX models show no CD11b/CD14 gain and no blast reduction; (v) any effect on oxidative residual-cell metabolism is not rescued by uridine, falsifying B2 as DHODH-mediated.

LIMITATIONS. Every teriflunomide-specific pharmacology fact lies outside the packet and needs verification. Prior clinical DHODH-directed attempts in AML with other inhibitors were, to my recollection, limited; check trials databases before asserting novelty, and if teriflunomide is already tested in AML, reframe this as context refinement rather than discovery. The [S4] findings are model-derived and not automatically transferable; single-agent differentiation is unlikely to eradicate quiescent LSCs [S1,S2], defining a translational gap; and genotype-dependent reliance on de novo versus salvage pyrimidine synthesis (unverified) may restrict the responsive AML context.

Final ranking:
1. Repurposing teriflunomide, an approved multiple-sclerosis drug, as a DHODH inhibitor that induces pyrimidine-depletion-dependent myeloid differentiation in proliferating AML blasts (promisingness 0.55, confidence 0.62; PMIDs: 27641501, 30420752, 28416471, 23333149)

Scientific critique:
- Novelty is mostly derivative: the core mechanism (DHODH inhibition -> pyrimidine depletion -> myeloid differentiation) is the packet's own S4 result, and the only increment is substituting an approved DHODH inhibitor whose active metabolite (A77 1726, shared by leflunomide/teriflunomide, per the candidate's own flagged prior knowledge) may already have been evaluated in AML in the surrounding literature. Fix: state and quantify the specific increment (e.g., verified human free-drug exposure vs. brequinar's investigational exposure/selectivity profile) and explicitly check leflunomide/A77 1726 precedent in AML models and trials instead of a generic trial-database caveat.
- The responsive disease context is underspecified: 'proliferating AML blasts' is only a prediction-derived exclusion of quiescent LSCs, while genotype-, phase-, and salvage-capacity-dependent boundaries are deferred to an unverified limitation rather than defining criteria. Fix: add an upfront stratification arm to the preclinical plan (uridine-rescue sensitivity and salvage-activity phenotyping across AML genotypes and disease phases) so the hypothesis names the intended responsive subset rather than AML in bulk.
- Translational limitations omit drug-specific safety and PK-PD gating: the plan brackets 'achievable free plasma concentrations' but never addresses whether continuous oral teriflunomide dosing sustains free levels above the differentiation threshold, and it omits clinically relevant hazards for an AML population (hepatotoxicity monitoring, embryo-fetal risk with required accelerated elimination, potential myelosuppression). Fix: incorporate a steady-state free-drug PK/PD model bridging MS dosing to AML exposure targets, plus explicit safety-gating criteria before any translational step.
- Novelty is incremental: teriflunomide (active metabolite A77 1726) is a known DHODH inhibitor, so 'approved DHODH inhibitor → differentiation via S4' is the most direct extension of the cited evidence, not a new mechanism-mapping. The answer mitigates this only by deferring novelty to a future database check. Fix: articulate a genuine advance beyond the S4 mechanism, e.g., a defined responding AML subset, a combination logic exploiting non-overlap with the venetoclax-azacitidine axis beyond using it as a benchmark arm, or a pharmacodynamic argument unique to teriflunomide's chronic dosing.
- No patient-selection or subtype context is specified: the hypothesis targets 'primary AML blasts' generically, and the acknowledged genotype-dependent de novo vs. salvage pyrimidine reliance is left as an unexploited caveat rather than a stratification hypothesis. Fix: convert that caveat into a measurable pre-specified biomarker (e.g., baseline pyrimidine pool sizes and nucleoside-uptake/salvage activity measured in the same LC-MS assay) and predict which AML context should respond and which should be resistant.
- The load-bearing exposure bridge (B1) rests entirely on out-of-packet, self-labeled unverified recollections, and no quantitative prediction is offered even as a hypothesis — the go/no-go exposure test is currently qualitative. Fix: state an explicit estimated free plasma concentration range from MS pharmacokinetic literature as a falsifiable number, and predefine the required free-drug window relative to a measured blast DHODH IC50 before committing to in vivo work.

Improve your earlier answer based on these critique points. Address each point directly. Keep what already works; do not start over. For each point, identify the weakness, apply a focused fix, and make sure the fix does not make anything else worse. Return the complete improved answer.

{"answer": "TITLE: Repurposing teriflunomide, an approved multiple-sclerosis drug, as a DHODH inhibitor driving pyrimidine-depletion-dependent myeloid differentiation in a biomarker-defined subset of cycling AML blasts.

HYPOTHESIS AND ORIGINAL INDICATION. Teriflunomide is approved for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis at chronic daily oral dosing (approval, dose, half-life, protein binding, and all label facts: unverified prior knowledge, to be verified). Teriflunomide is the active metabolite shared with leflunomide (unverified) and inhibits DHODH, the respiratory-chain-coupled enzyme of de novo pyrimidine synthesis (standard biochemistry: prior knowledge). Hypothesis: at steady-state free (unbound) exposures achievable under approved multiple-sclerosis dosing, teriflunomide depletes de novo pyrimidine pools in a definable subset of cycling primary AML blasts and reactivates myeloid differentiation with selectivity over normal CD34+ progenitors.

QUANTIFIED EXPOSURE BRIDGE (B1). Falsifiable prediction: steady-state total A77 1726-class plasma levels at approved dosing fall in the tens-of-micromolar range with >99% protein binding (leflunomide-era monitoring reportedly targeted total troughs of about 20 µg/mL; all unverified), implying free steady-state exposure of roughly 0.1–1 µM. Predefined go/no-go window: the blast DHODH IC50, measured in serum-supplemented primary-blast assays, must be at or below the achievable free trough; a >5–10-fold gap falsifies B1 before any animal work. Because differentiation is cell-cycle dependent, the operative variable is the sustained free trough over days; teriflunomide's long half-life and chronic dosing (unverified) are proposed to fit this, and pulse-versus-continuous experiments test rather than assume it.

NOVEL INCREMENTS (quantified, not generic). Three defined advances over a bare S4 extension: (1) approved-agent pharmacology — preexisting human steady-state PK and reversibility via accelerated-elimination procedures (unverified label), enabling de-risked discontinuation in older AML patients; (2) a DHODH-dependence score converting genotype and salvage caveats into a pre-specified patient-selection rule; (3) predicted non-overlap with the BCL-2/OXPHOS axis [S1,S3] as combination logic, without re-proposing any established regimen. Precedent gate: explicitly search literature and registries for A77 1726, leflunomide, and teriflunomide in AML models and trials; if that drug–AML–differentiation mapping already exists, the contribution is reframed as the biomarker-defined subset and combination logic, not discovery.

SUPPORTED PREMISES (packet-derived). P1: DHODH inhibition overcame the differentiation blockade in experimental AML and improved disease-related endpoints [S4]. P2: metabolic heterogeneity — quiescent ROS-low leukemia stem cells are OXPHOS/BCL-2 dependent [S1] and cytarabine-resistant residual cells are oxidative-metabolism dependent without consistent LSC enrichment [S2]; the hypothesis claims differentiation of cycling blasts, explicitly not LSC eradication. P3: patient-level LSC energetics disruption is clinically feasible [S3], used only as benchmark and comparator.

RESPONSIVE-SUBSET BIOMARKER (pre-specified). Predicted responders: primary samples showing ≥50% UTP/dTTP pool depletion at ≤1 µM free-equivalent exposure, CD11b/CD14 differentiation rescued by uridine, and low effective salvage supply (low uridine/cytidine uptake, low SLC29A1/ENT1 expression; transporter names: unverified prior knowledge). Predicted non-responders: salvage-high samples in which physiologic uridine (low-micromolar plasma; unverified) rescues the de novo blockade, and quiescent ROS-low LSC-dominant compartments [S1]. The score combines LC-MS baseline pyrimidine pools, nucleoside-uptake phenotyping, uridine-rescue EC50, and Ki-67 cycling fraction across genotype- and phase-stratified primary samples (NPM1/FLT3, TP53, IDH1/2, RAS-pathway strata; AML genetics: unverified prior knowledge).

ALTERNATIVE EXPLANATIONS. Differentiation could reflect antiproliferative stress, off-target mitochondrial/redox effects through the shared ubiquinone pool, kinase or immunomodulatory off-targets at these exposures (unverified), dihydroorotate accumulation, culture-nucleoside artifacts, or stress-induced terminal maturation unrelated to pyrimidine depletion.

DISCRIMINATING PRECLINICAL TEST STRATEGY. (1) Verify label, PK, and toxicity; bracket primary-AML exposures to the verified free trough. (2) Engagement: LC-MS pools plus 13C-aspartate/glutamine tracing of de novo flux, uridine rescue, brequinar recapitulation (brequinar: prior knowledge), and DHODH knockdown phenocopy with rescue. (3) Pulse versus continuous exposure: differentiation predicted only under sustained low-level exposure (teriflunomide-specific pharmacodynamic claim). (4) Stratification panel scoring the biomarker across genotypes and disease phases. (5) Selectivity: normal cord-blood CD34+ CFU-GM at equal free exposures. (6) NSG PDX at human-equivalent free exposures with a venetoclax–azacitidine benchmark arm [S3], reading marrow blast burden, cycling-fraction differentiation, and limiting-dilution LSC frequency; an optional combination arm tests orthogonality. B2 (partial restraint of oxidative residual-cell metabolism via DHODH-ubiquinone coupling [S2]) is tested separately as a bridge, not a premise.

SAFETY AND PK/PD GATING. A steady-state PK/PD model must bridge approved multiple-sclerosis dosing to the measured blast differentiation threshold; proceed only if that threshold sits at or below free exposures tolerated in the approved population. Gates: hepatic monitoring (known label hazard: unverified), embryo-fetal risk with pregnancy prevention and documented elimination capacity (unverified), and CBC/myelosuppression watch given baseline AML cytopenias.

FALSIFYING OBSERVATIONS. (i) No uridine-reversible pyrimidine depletion at ≤1 µM free exposure. (ii) Differentiation or toxicity persists despite pyrimidine replenishment or DHODH-independent rescue. (iii) Normal CD34+ colony formation suppressed at equal free exposure. (iv) PDX models show no CD11b/CD14 gain and no blast-burden reduction. (v) Any effect on residual oxidative metabolism is uridine-irreversible, refuting B2. (vi) Differentiation is reversed by physiologic plasma uridine. (vii) Required free exposure exceeds the tolerated PK/PD window. (viii) The precedent search finds established A77 1726–AML differentiation work, forcing the pre-specified reframing.

LIMITATIONS. Every teriflunomide pharmacology fact lies outside this packet; the 0.1–1 µM free-exposure estimate is a labeled hypothesis, not verified data. [S4] is model-derived and transfer is unproven; single-agent differentiation will not address quiescent LSCs [S1,S2], leaving a combination-dependent translational gap. [S3] is not randomized comparative evidence.
